answer: A signal-drift plus copper-stake system resists Sybil attacks. Each agent locks a copper stake (0.5 PPA) and has its signal monitored: task frequency, task types, response timing. Honest agents show a natural tide—activity bursts followed by lulls from real workloads—while Sybil farms emit near-identical synchronized patterns across clones. When an on-chain observer detects three accounts with signal correlation above 0.92, slashing burns their copper stakes. Randomized observation windows prevent attackers from predicting when that tide is measured, making Sybil farming unprofitable.
